_doc: T-1158. Which tier every attribute of every household and person stands on - attested, inferred, reconstructed, or unknown, meaning nothing is asserted yet - together with every genuinely reconstructed value and the basis it rests on. DERIVED from the committed cards: rebuild with --build, and --check refuses a hand-edit and a card that has moved under it. renderers/web/js/attribute-tiers.js derives the same tier for the card a visitor opens, and tools/check_attribute_tiers.mjs holds the two answers together.

reconstructed.note: NOT AN ARRIVAL DATE, AND THE RECORD HAD NONE AT ALL. The recovered v4 research places William H. Adams on an 1835 Chicago poll list; it does not say when the poll was taken, and nothing in the corpus says when he came. The only thing the evidence bears is that he was in Chicago at some point during 1835, so the value carried here is the last day that evidence can reach, at 'not_later_than' precision — the same shape the town's letter-list arrivals take, and a bound rather than a date. Whether he was standing here on 1 July 1835 is the open question present_on_scene_date records as uncertain. The block arrived from PR #670 with a null value and no precision, which the gate could not read.

reconstructed.note: NOT ATTESTED IN ANYTHING THIS PROJECT HOLDS. Dole's New England origin and his Detroit connection through Oliver Newberry are widely repeated in the Chicago literature and could not be traced to a source in this dataset, so the value is carried as a conjecture, cites nothing, and is flagged for a later parcel to settle or delete. T-0396 WEAKENS THIS FURTHER (2026-09-12) AND IT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY KEPT: half of the received story is the partnership with Oliver Newberry of Detroit, and that partnership is now REFUSED — the firm's own card prints Oliver Newberry as its Detroit reference, not as its partner. So 'by way of Detroit' has lost the one thing the literature offered in its support. The value is left standing because it was already `reconstructed`, cites nothing, and is flagged for a later parcel to settle or delete; this note is the reason that parcel should expect to delete it.

What is claimed is the street FACE and nothing narrower — no lot, no roof, no door count, and no corner even where the volume prints one — and the grade is `reconstructed`, this dataset's word for a figure the reconstruction supplies rather than a source. North Water Street stands in 1835 under that name and in that place, and the entry prints it as this person's home. So the placement is the FACE and nothing narrower, and no roof is dealt. A home is carried back on a weaker argument than a shop is: a shopfront is capital sunk into one street's trade and a lodging is a month's rent, which is why this policy claims less than docs/ADDRESS-BACK-PROJECTION.md does from the same volume. The rule is docs/RESIDENCE-BACK-PROJECTION.md and the liberty is L223; a reader who thinks 9 years is too far to carry a house should read the grade as the disagreement being invited.
